### Wire format

Only these types write different bytes than with rc.1:

- A `[NinoType]` struct of another assembly whose members are auto-properties (a positional `record struct`, for
  example) is now copied as raw memory in every build. rc.1 did so when the struct was seen as source (the IDE, a
  project reference), but wrote it member by member from a package or a command-line build. A struct, array or list
  holding such a struct can therefore differ from an rc.1 package or command-line build where the struct has padding
  (#200).
- `nint` and `nuint` members are serialized on netstandard (Unity included), as 8 bytes. rc.1 skipped them there with
  NINO007.

### New

- `[assembly: NinoTypeLayout]` describes how each `[NinoType]` is written, for compatibility checks between builds
  (#197). [Layout Metadata](https://nino.xgamedev.net/en/docs/v4/evolving-data#layout-metadata)
- `NinoRegistry.Remove(assembly)` clears what Nino cached for an assembly, so a collectible `AssemblyLoadContext` can
  unload it; on .NET 8 and later this runs when the context unloads (#199).
  [Unloading Assemblies](https://nino.xgamedev.net/en/docs/v4/platforms#unloading-assemblies)
- `new NinoArrayBufferWriter(initialCapacity, pool)` rents from your `ArrayPool<byte>` (#198).

### Fixes

- Two `[NinoFormerName]` on one type are reported as error NINO026; the generator took the first and
  `NinoTypeId.Of` threw `AmbiguousMatchException` (#201).

Every change between v4 releases: [Changelog](https://nino.xgamedev.net/en/docs/v4/changelog).
